Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing, condensed

Symbols, rules, datums and every geometric tolerance, with key concepts, formulas and figures. Follows the 27 chapters of Krulikowski's Fundamentals of GD&T, 3rd ed. (ASME Y14.5-2009).

Separate topic · materials science & selection

Materials, condensed

Properties, the science behind them, and how to choose materials for stiffness, strength, toughness, fatigue, heat, creep, corrosion and electrical use. Chapters 4–15 of Ashby, Shercliff & Cebon, Materials: Engineering, Science, Processing and Design, 4th ed.

— chapters— sections— formulas— key figuresMaterial indices & charts
Course notes · 24-673 Soft Robotics

Soft Robotics, condensed

Artificial muscle and skin, soft materials and modeling, fabrication, shape memory and stiffness tuning, medical robots, simulation, adhesion, haptics and locomotion: condensed from the 12 lectures of 24-673 Soft Robotics (Prof. C. Majidi), with key slide figures.

— lectures— sections— equations— key figuresInterview problems
Separate topic · built around a Tesla patent application

Tactile Sensing, condensed

The mechanical engineering behind a formed, soft tactile skin: materials, contact, elastomers, transduction, laminates, thermoforming, interfaces and manufacturing. Structure follows US 2026/0310299 A1 (Tesla, Three-Dimensional Soft Compliant Array Tactile Sensor); bullets marked "In the patent" come from it, and the theory, equations and typical property values are standard mechanics background.

— chapters— sections— equations— key figuresUS 2026/0310299 A1
Course notes · 27-577/777 Advanced Polymer Science & Engineering

Polymers, condensed

The structure–processing–properties relationships of solid polymers, following the 11 topics of the course syllabus: chain models, the amorphous, semicrystalline and liquid-crystalline states, rubber elasticity, viscoelasticity, processing and orientation, and the Flory–Huggins thermodynamics of blends. Built from the Fall 2021 lecture notes, with depth, figures and exercises from Gedde, Polymer Physics (primary) and McCrum, Buckley & Bucknall, Principles of Polymer Engineering (secondary).

Course27-577 (9 units) | 27-777 (12 units), Fall 2021, Tue/Thu 12:20–2:10 PM
LecturerProf. Michael R. Bockstaller
TextsGedde, Polymer Physics (primary); McCrum et al., 2nd ed., and Osswald & Menges (secondary)

Krulikowski, Fundamentals of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing, 3rd ed. (Cengage, 2012) and M. Ashby, H. Shercliff & D. Cebon, Materials: Engineering, Science, Processing and Design, 4th ed. (Butterworth-Heinemann, 2019); Soft Robotics notes are condensed from the lecture slides of 24-673 Soft Robotics (Prof. C. Majidi); for private study. The Tactile Sensing notes are organized around US patent application publication 2026/0310299 A1 (Tesla, Inc.), with independently written mechanics background, problems and figures. The Polymers notes follow the 27-577/777 syllabus and lecture notes (Prof. M. R. Bockstaller), with figures and exercises from U. W. Gedde, Polymer Physics (Kluwer) and N. G. McCrum, C. P. Buckley & C. B. Bucknall, Principles of Polymer Engineering, 2nd ed. (Oxford University Press).
